## ps2/BATTLE_NAVIGATION
# Experimental Battle navigation

## Player acceptance

A bot must pursue a moving opponent around track obstacles without abandoning
its human controllers or native weapon, damage, scoring and respawn lifecycle.
A usable result requires rendered movement on the named track plus native
state showing progress, attacks, recovery and a completed five-kill match.
A racing-line waypoint or a passing CPU fixture does not prove obstacle clearance.

## Reused native course

The implementation in `src/battle_navigation.cpp` reads the loaded native
primary course. It does not create an arena, move track geometry or invent a
collision-query ABI. `docs/BATTLE_RECOVERY.md` records the prior-art review:
Road Trip Adventure's deterministic scripted-input/capture method is reused;
its different game structures cannot supply EOD navigation or collision calls.
A fresh source check at pinned revision
`0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8` inspected the repository tree,
[`Driving.cpp`](https://github.com/silentsudin/RoadTripAdventure-recomp/blob/0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8/src/game/Driving.cpp)
and [`overrides.cpp`](https://github.com/silentsudin/RoadTripAdventure-recomp/blob/0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8/src/game/overrides.cpp).
The relevant wheel there is native player-controller interception with
script/analogue-input separation (controller `0x0021A820`), not an EOD course
reader or obstacle-query ABI. Reuse the interception/test principle; do not
copy its controller address or invent compatible collision structures.

The cache at EE `0x003CD190` has up to three 12-byte records, followed by its
count at `0x003CD1B4`. Only a unique active type `0x101` record is accepted.
Its relocated resource must have tag `0x104F128B`, header size 48 and node size
60. Primary count is the high halfword of `+0x1C` (halfword `+0x1E`); root is
`+0x20`. Nodes are contiguous: X/Z position at `+0/+4`, X/Z tangent at
`+8/+0xC`, next pointer at `+0x14`, and section length at `+0x18`.
**Node `+0x10` is packed metadata, not a previous pointer.**

Native `0x0013AF20` indexes this primary array modulo its count;
`0x00139B60` steps backward by 60 and wraps at that count. Secondary branch
lists at node `+0x38` are deliberately excluded. Reinspect these guest addresses
in locally generated source/disassembly; no retail code or resource is committed.

Pointers/spans, count, resource identity, ownership, finite coordinates, lengths
and closed next links are validated. Missing, malformed, ambiguous or unowned
resources discard the cached course and use direct pursuit. Event construction
resets navigation state. A stable resource identity reuses its validated snapshot.

## Policy and limits

The car and opponent project onto primary course segments. Within 35 world
units of both projections, a bot follows a shorter course arc using bounded
lookahead and direction hysteresis. Near opponents on the same local section
use direct interception. At crossings, the car's heading helps disambiguate
projection; this does not establish a traversable connection between branches.
Only steering aim and the turn-speed limit use the waypoint. Native weapon aim,
range and elevation still refer to the actual opponent.

This is **course following plus direct pursuit**, not general pathfinding.
It cannot check a segment for walls, choose native secondary branches, route
safely through arbitrary infields or guarantee escape from every pin. Reverse
recovery remains a bounded steering heuristic. Home has no supported primary
course in the baseline capture, so its behavior is direct pursuit/recovery.
All bots remain experimental until the player acceptance above is established
on each relevant map. Unlocking a map does not certify navigation there.

## Solo map decision

Do not claim that map size determines eligibility. A small arena can have
impassable barriers; a larger oval can provide a useful native course. Keep
solo exposure bounded to existing native Battle descriptors and safe native
menu capacity. The current 312/320 contest occupancy leaves eight additions:
Anoka, Ashland, Baxter, Dennison, Dundas, Eagan, Gilroy and Hampton. This is a
capacity policy, not a tested small-track allowlist. Home/Mankato/Woodly remain
native multiplayer selections; unlocking them does not expand the solo table.
Anoka now has bounded final-policy five-kill/results evidence; that does not
validate every obstacle route. Safe per-map eligibility needs full chase/completion evidence before widening
solo exposure or claiming any current map to be fully validated.

## Rejected obstacle-query candidates

Read-only native inspection recovered segment/BSP routine `0x00216D98`:
`a0=start XYZ*`, `a1=end XYZ*`, `a2=hit XYZ output*`, `v0=hit boolean`,
root pointer at `0x003D1C24`, hit triangle at `0x00496218`. However, saved
Home/Woodly/Dennison worlds each contain one giant horizontal ground triangle
and no child nodes. Their installed `track.bsp` resources are only 108 bytes.
The substantial scenery collision resources are `track.bsc` (SCOL), not this
fallback BSP. A correct call to that routine would still miss the fences.

The static proxy list at `0x003D216C` is incomplete too: Woodly has nineteen
BOX proxies far from the observed final pins, while Home has zero. Neither
candidate was integrated or shipped as a general wall-clearance oracle.

The next discriminating research observation would be a read-only trace of
actual native impulse/contact entry `0x0017B918`, matched against an actual
bot body, followed by identifying the blocking SCOL/shape. Native input
registers there are body `a0`, other shape `a1`, impulse XYZ pointer `a2`,
contact XYZ pointer `a3`, type `t0`, optional alternate point `t1`, other body
`t2`, and impulse scale `f12`; it queues contact then calls `0x0017B818`.
A candidate host logger was written but never built or executed and was removed
 This is a future probe, not a validated navigation API.

## Reproduction and diagnostics

Run games and builds sequentially, muted and headless. With an owned installed
disc, the authored harness saves isolated configuration, memory card, exact
controller scripts, captures, native trace and final RAM under ignored `work/`:

```sh
tools/test_battle.sh "$DISC" mixed work/battle-home 12000 Home
tools/test_battle.sh "$DISC" mixed work/battle-woodly 12000 Woodly
tools/test_battle.sh "$DISC" mixed work/battle-dennison 12000 Dennison
python3 tools/analyze_battle_trace.py work/battle-woodly --output work/battle-woodly/summary.json
```

The harness sets `EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1`, `--headless`, 1x Vulkan,
FrameSkip=0 and native blast multipliers. `EOD_BATTLE_TRACE` opts into sampled
`BATTLE_ROUTE` lines with `course`, `routing`, opponent and slot. This records
whether course following actually ran. Require the matching loaded `.trk`
resource and rendered menu label, rather than trusting the output directory.
Sampled firing transitions and low-progress intervals are evidence summaries,
not exact shot counts or a collision/acceptance oracle. Capture inspection and
native phase/score/lifecycle state remain necessary.


## ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY
# Battle mode, chicken weapons and AI contracts

Status: experimental bot policy; native CPU contracts and bounded live Battle evidence verified on
2026-10-19; complete-match and lifecycle acceptance are tracked below. This chapter supersedes conflicting weapon, input,
registry and respawn claims in [the historical gameplay notes](GAMEPLAY_MODS_RE.md).
It describes the North American `SLUS_209.10` executable only. Addresses are
guest EE addresses, not host pointers or portable APIs for another game.
Executable SHA-256: `4f60053dc141365f5ae50737622f8408be30ced513b4c109427c926461f2e2ae`.

## Final bounded scope — 2026-10-19

The owner stopped further expansion at the tested checkpoint and authorized
building, publishing main and removing verified obsolete builds/merged unused
branches. This ships the measured native weapon recovery and experimental bot
policy; it is not a claim that every original acceptance ambition below is met.
No numeric participant selector, Career exclusion, new obstacle query or native
versus mod flag-ownership redesign was implemented. `BattleBots` remains a
boolean that fills Battle to four cars while preserving humans. Changes apply
when starting the next event, not by restarting the app. Native behavior applies
when it is off. That does not mean "humans only": native `0x0012C158`
uses `max(humans, min(contest.max_cars, native_cap))`, with observed native
caps 99/10/4/4 for one/two/three/four humans. A native Battle descriptor with
`max_cars=2` therefore yields two cars for one or two humans, then three/four
for three/four humans. Solo with bots off does not receive the custom AI weapon
or input policy; that particular gameplay journey was not live-validated.
Ordinary non-Battle rosters bypass that hook. `SinglePlayerBattle`
still appends native Battle descriptors in solo Action **and Career** where
capacity permits; disable it for unchanged native Career contest menus. A Career
season hard lock was discussed but not added at this stopping point.

Unbuilt contact/weapon tracing candidates and unfinished toggle test fixtures
were preserved under ignored `work/stopped-expansion-2026-10-19/`, then removed
from the shipped source. The original inherited recovery backup is preserved.
Known limitations and the exact verified journeys below remain authoritative.

## Player success and acceptance

The player can enter original two-player Battle with independent controls and
visible native chickens. A shot follows the car's orientation, collides and
explodes, attributes the hit to the correct player, and reloads on the original
timer and release/repress sequence. Optional bots must preserve every human
controller and complete the same native lifecycle: drive, attack, recover,
shoot, respawn, score and finish a match. Native track geometry and spawn
transforms remain authoritative.

Required evidence combines instruction/ABI inspection, focused native tests,
rendered gameplay, scripted inputs and RAM state. Passing a mock input test or
seeing a nonzero velocity does not prove visible player success. The bounded
recovery targets at most four participants; increasing the native participant
capacity requires separate structural work.

## What reverse engineering and recompilation establish

**Reverse engineering** here means recovering the executable's contracts from
instructions, call sites, memory writes and observed behavior. Labels such as
"body", "interface" and "owner" are descriptions supported by those uses;
they are not recovered original C++ declarations.

**Disassembly** exposes the original MIPS instructions. **Decompilation** would
reconstruct higher-level source from them, without guaranteeing the original
variable names, types or structure. This investigation uses the disassembler
and the project's generated translation as evidence; it is not a recovered
original-source release.

**Static recompilation** translates guest instructions into host-compiled code
which still operates on the guest register state and memory. Generated
`f_0017E000(void)` therefore receives its arguments through `g_ee`, not through
ordinary host C++ parameters. The generated function and native MIPS function
share a guest address identity, but successful compilation alone does not prove
correct runtime semantics.

**Modding** intentionally changes behavior around that baseline. Extra blast
force, custom bots or a different launch mode are modifications, not evidence
that the original weapon has been restored. Keep native acceptance and optional
mod acceptance distinct. Do not repair a guessed ABI by adding more guessed
state writes.

## Native address evidence

Evidence was inspected in locally generated `gen/rec_020.c`, `gen/rec_021.c` and
`gen/rec_023.c`, with the guest addresses below as stable lookup keys. Generated
file partitioning can change. Source checkout at the initial focused test run:
`67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7` plus the uncommitted recovery changes.
This is a provenance checkpoint, not a claim that this commit alone contains
the recovery.

| Guest function / site | Observed contract | Evidence scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0x0017DE30` | Registers interface `$a0`, owner index `$a1`, slot `$a2` into a 12-byte row. | Generated native stores. |
| `0x0017DE78` | Queries owner `$a0` and slot `$a1`; returns the row's interface in `$v0`, or zero. | Generated comparison and return paths. |
| `0x0017EA10`, registration call near `0x0017EB98` | Initialization registers `body+0x1DC`, owner from `body+0x1E8`, slot zero. | Native initializer; not covered by the focused fixture. |
| `0x0017DFA8` | Allocates a `0x228`-byte body and performs constructor work. | Does not establish that allocation alone completes gameplay initialization. |
| `0x0017E000` | Trigger takes interface `$a0`, car body `$a1`, input pointer `$a2`; subtracts `0x1DC` from interface. | Executed by focused test. |
| `0x0017AF80` | Copies a 48-byte pose into body+`0x64`, then propagates scene/bounds state. | Native copy executed; downstream propagation stubbed. |
| `0x0017E4D8` | With master and weapon enabled, stores state zero and deadline `now+3`. | Executed by focused test. |
| `0x0017E5C8`, `0x0017E5F8`–`0x0017E624` | Native update advances expired cooldown to release-waiting state. | Timer path executed; downstream physics/render work stubbed. |
| `0x0018FC1C`–`0x0018FCB8` within `0x0018F2A8` | Human driver gates on master+weapon, queries by controller+`0x40` owner index, reads L2 and calls interface vtable+8 with car and input pointer. | Native caller inspection; full driver not executed by focused test. |
| `0x0017E718`, call at `0x0017E7FC` | Detonation passes body+`0x88` position and body+`0x1E8` attacker index to `0x0017DA58`. | Native caller inspection; damage/score acceptance pending. |
| `0x0017DA58` | Resolves attacker index through `0x00179A08` before the native radial impulse path. | Ownership flow inspected; not exercised by focused fixture. |
| `0x0018AA80` | Stores steering `$f12` at car+`0x1B6C`. | Native setter inspection. Writing car+`0x1B80` is not this steering contract. |

Reinspect locally with a local executable and analysis metadata present:

```sh
.venv/bin/python tools/dis.py -f 0017DE78
.venv/bin/python tools/dis.py -f 0017E000
.venv/bin/python tools/dis.py -f 0017E4D8
.venv/bin/python tools/dis.py -f 0017E5C8
.venv/bin/python tools/dis.py -f 0017E718
.venv/bin/python tools/dis.py -f 0018AA80
```

Do not commit the executable, generated functions, RAM dumps, captures or
binaries. Commit authored tests, extraction tools and interpreted findings.

## Registry, body and input ABI

The registry starts at `0x003CE3F8`, with count at `0x003CE4B8`. A row contains:

| Row offset | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `+0x00` | Owner/car **index**, not a car pointer. |
| `+0x04` | Weapon slot. Native chicken initialization uses zero. |
| `+0x08` | Weapon interface pointer. For this chicken, `interface = body+0x1DC`. |

The trigger reads a 32-bit pressed value at `$a2`; the native human caller
provides a two-word input structure with the second word zero. Forward both
pressed and released input through the native call. A call to `0x0017E5C8`
does not replace the trigger, and writing body offsets relative to a registry
interface corrupts a different memory region.

Relevant body fields are:

| Body offset | Meaning used by the inspected routines |
| --- | --- |
| `+0x7C` | Forward vector after native pose copy. |
| `+0x88` | World position. |
| `+0x94` | Identifier copied from the car by the trigger. |
| `+0x104` | Launch/linear velocity vector. |
| `+0x1DC` | Weapon interface/vtable location. |
| `+0x1E0` | Trigger state: 0 cooldown, 1 awaiting release, 2 armed. |
| `+0x1E4` | Cooldown deadline, float. |
| `+0x1E8` | Registered owner index; preserved by firing. |
| `+0x1F4` | In-flight marker. |
| `+0x210`, `+0x214`, `+0x218` | Effect object pointers used across initialization/flight/detonation. |
| `+0x21C` | Local muzzle offset, three floats. |

The native initializer establishes more than the registry entry: it assigns
ownership, initializes scene state and attaches effects. Allocation followed by
handwritten registry rows and a fabricated ready flag is not an equivalent
initialization path. Use the existing native lifecycle and query its interface.

## Straight Battle, feat mortar and rain

The active mask is `0x003C4190`:

| Bits | Consequence in the inspected paths |
| --- | --- |
| Master `0x1` and weapon `0x8` | Native human weapon dispatch and three-second cooldown enabled. |
| Master and `0x10` | Feat mortar launch branch. This is not required for a straight Battle shot. |
| Master and `0x80` | Rain velocity branch, checked before the mortar branch. |

Let `F` and `U` be the pose's forward/up vectors and `V` the car velocity.
The native trigger computes:

- Straight Battle: `F * (length(V) + 28)`.
- Feat mortar: `(F * 0.707 + U * 0.4949) * 24.888889 + V`, with native float
  constants and instruction-order rounding.
- Rain branch: `(0, -19.62, 0)`.

These are initial velocities, not a promise of gravity-free or collision-free
flight. A sideways or reversing car contributes its speed magnitude to the
straight shot; mortar adds the velocity vector. Pitch affects the straight
shot because it follows the car's forward axis. The native trigger also
transforms the muzzle offset by the car pose before launching.

Default blast force and radius multipliers are now one; existing saved values
remain configurable and are not silently overwritten.

For the straight optional Chicken Fight mod, master+weapon is `0x09`; forcing
`0x19` selects mortar. If turbo is also enabled, the corresponding straight-shot
mask is `0x0B`, before unrelated flags. Preserve the distinction between flags
owned by the optional mod and flags established by native Battle/feat selection.

## Reload and release/repress

The native clock is a float at `0x003CDACC`. With master+weapon enabled, firing
sets state zero and deadline `now+3`. The update changes state zero to one only
when `now > deadline`; equality does not expire it. Held input leaves state one
waiting. Released input changes one to two without firing. A subsequent pressed
input in state two fires and starts a new cooldown.

Early release/repress during cooldown does not bypass the timer. In-flight state
is separate from trigger state: the original trigger does not use it as an
additional ready gate. Do not introduce a different reload model by equating
in-flight with cooldown or by manually resetting either field. Collision,
detonation and reset paths own the remaining projectile lifecycle.

## Focused tests and verified results

[`extract_native_weapon_reference.py`] (`../tools/extract_native_weapon_reference.py`, source checkout)
reuses the existing movie-bit reference extraction approach. At build time it
extracts locally generated `0x0017E000`, `0x0017E4D8`, `0x0017E5C8` and
`0x0017AF80` into the build directory. The checked-in
[`native_weapon_test.cpp`] (`../tests/native_weapon_test.cpp`, source checkout) contains synthetic
inputs and authored assertions, not copied retail functions.

Scene/bounds propagation `0x0017A498` and per-frame physics/render work
`0x0017F4E0` / `0x0017BBC0` are boundary stubs. None changes weapon state or
velocity. Unexpected owner lookup, rain spawn or hidden-pose update paths fail
the test. The native trigger, timer state transitions and pose copy stay real.

```sh
EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1 cmake --build build-mac --target native_weapon_test -j2
EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1 ctest --test-dir build-mac \
  -R '^native_chicken_weapon$' --output-on-failure -V
```

The initial coordinated run passed **138 checks in 0.26 seconds**. Cases cover
stationary launch, lateral/reverse speed, quarter turn, oblique yaw, pitch,
transformed muzzle position, flag gating/precedence, cooldown equality/expiry,
held suppression, release/repress, preserved owner and effect activation.

This is a native behavior characterization test. It does not itself execute the
production mod's flag-selection hook or full HumanDriver path. Separate wrapper
tests must prove those integrations. It also does not prove initialization,
rendered flight, collision, explosion damage/credit, reset, respawn or a complete
match. Retaining an owner integer in a fixture is weaker evidence than observing
correct scoring after a real hit.

## Prior art and evidence method

Checked [Road Trip Adventure's development guide at revision
`0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8`](https://github.com/silentsudin/RoadTripAdventure-recomp/blob/0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8/docs/DEVELOPING.md).
Its regression approach combines deterministic guest time, scripted pad input,
headless execution, exact frame capture and RAM observations. Reuse that method
of connecting an input to observable state and pictures. Its game structures,
addresses and driving model belong to a different executable and are not EOD
weapon or Battle contracts. No Road Trip game structure is copied here.

EOD already has `tools/padscript.py`, independent `EOD_PAD_SCRIPT` and
`EOD_PAD_SCRIPT1`, bounded `--frames` runs, screenshot output and `EOD_DUMP_RAM`
at exit. `tools/test_2p_race.sh` demonstrates independent scripted controllers;
its race navigation sequence is not a Battle acceptance test. Keep a dedicated
Battle script and exact configuration with each result. Do not call EOD runs
bit-identical merely because the input schedule repeats; establish that property
with measured state/frame comparisons first.

Automated builds and game runs must be coordinated, headless and muted. Use
`EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1`, plus `--headless` for the game. Start native baseline
validation at 1x PS2 resolution, 4:3, original timing and no frame skipping.
Archive local evidence under ignored work/build directories, not the repository.

## Native Battle construction and bot policy

Battle event ID is `0x18000224`. The current event is `0x003CF19C`, and the
master pointer is `0x003CF194` (Battle vtable `0x003F7770`). The master is
`0x5AC` bytes with **four** `0x50`-byte participant records starting at `+0x454`.
Rankings start at `+0x594`, spawn index at `+0x5A4`, and participant count at
`+0x5A8`. Increasing count beyond four overwrites adjacent state. Other race
arrays having twenty entries does not expand Battle's records, rankings or HUD.
Faster host hardware does not remove these structural constraints.

The optional `BattleBots` setting fills to four participants before native roster
construction (`0x0012C158`), allowing `0x0012AEF0`, `0x00111E10` and
`0x001116E0` to select valid native vehicles and driver records. Participant
records are at description+`0x2C`, stride `0x78`: type `0x50` identifies a human,
`0x51` identifies AI. **Human slots are not necessarily first.** Live solo
construction has put its human in slot 3; mixed construction has put humans in
slots 2 and 3. Human count and viewport count cannot identify a particular car.
The AI slot mask is latched at event construction, so UI changes take effect on
the next event.

After `0x0020FD48` builds the world, missing AI weapons are created through
`0x00227EE8(slot)`, the same scene factory used by native humans. It derives
muzzle offsets from the model, creates the explosive chicken scene and queues
physical construction through `0x00213578 / 0x001758B8`. `0x0017EA10` registers
the physical interface later. Capacity accounting must reserve queued entries;
checking only the current registry count is insufficient. Bounds are sixteen
weapon records and 1,200 world/visible object pointers. Existing scene/weapon
ownership and native suppression `0x002CE180` are respected.

Battle's native AI factory chooses a NullDriver. It does not register with the
normal driver update list; hooking its empty update function produced no live
inputs even though an isolated wrapper test passed. The policy therefore runs
after native AICar update `0x001A2D20`, once per actual car update. Native physics,
damage, scene updates and human drivers still run. The policy selects a living
opponent with hysteresis, leads moving targets, steers toward contact, slows for
turns, reverses when stuck and fires only when aim/range/elevation permit. It
uses native weapon input and cooldown instead of changing weapon state.
This is a custom pursuit/ramming policy, not recovered original Battle AI.

### Correct vehicle controls

| Car offset | Native setter | Meaning/evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `+0x1B6C` | `0x0018AA78/80` | Steering target. Physics smooths into `+0x1B80`; that latter field is not the input setter. |
| `+0x1B70` | `0x0018AA70` | Throttle input. |
| `+0x1B74` | `0x0018AA68` | Brake input. |
| `+0x1B78` | `0x0018AA60` | Drivetrain engagement input: native Derby writes **1** through `0x001975B0 → 0x001988E8`. Setting zero prevented useful bot acceleration in a live test. “Clutch” is an inferred label, not an original symbol. |
| `+0x1B7C` | `0x0018AA58` | Rear brake/handbrake input. Physics multiplies it by eight and combines it with the rear braking terms. |
| `+0x1B90` | `0x0018AA50` | Requested gear; `-10` is native automatic forward selection, `-1` reverse. |

Earlier claims that `+0x1B78` is the handbrake are incorrect. Native Human and
Derby callers, physics consumers, and live RAM comparison agree on the corrected
separation. A nonzero throttle field alone did not establish working driving.

### Death, scoring and respawn

Common Car damage already reports death through
`0x0018D6C0 → 0x001DA468 → BattleMaster virtual +0x60 → 0x00166F48`.
This works for AI without NullDriver forwarding. Do not report it twice.
The participant record's dead flag is master+`0x458 + slot*0x50`, death time
`+0x45C`, kills `+0x460`, deaths `+0x464`, suicide penalties `+0x468`.
Displayed/net score is **kills minus suicide penalties**. `0x00167D58` changes
phase 1 (combat) to phase 2 (finished) at five net kills; phase 0 is countdown.

Humans see “Press the SELECT button to respawn.” Bots request the same native
operation, `0x001671E8(master,slot)`, while dead and combat is active. It checks
the native strict two-second delay before calling `0x001675C0`, which resets the
car through `0x00189F50`, chooses a native track spawn with `0x001673B8`, applies
it through the car's virtual reset, and resets event presentation. The bridge
does not invent spawn coordinates or directly clear death/score fields.

Initial placement also has a common native path:
`0x00185470 → 0x00187248 → 0x00187688 → 0x001D92A8 → 0x001DA418 → 0x00167C70`.
Do not infer that all AI need a manual teleport because their driver is NullDriver.
Native Derby uses a separate bound resource loaded through `0x00151BA0`;
Battle's bound pointer `0x003CD580` was zero in live runs. Substituting Derby
controllers without constructing their dependencies is unsafe.

### Solo menu exposure

`SinglePlayerBattle` appends a contest referencing an existing native VAL Battle
section after the outer `0x001244A8` loader returns. It preserves every existing
race, VAL key/value string and native `c_battle` track layout. The native caller
then sorts/remaps through `0x001248E0`. There is no world-origin arena, shared
string overwrite or replacement of a track's first race.

Native limits are forty Eves, thirty-two contests per Eve, and 320 total
contests. The observed solo resource set already contained 312 contests. The
bridge fills remaining capacity in display-name order; consequently Battle
availability is bounded by the loaded resource set, not guaranteed for every
track. Expanding the table or safely constructing a separate Battle menu is
future work. This capacity limit must not be silently bypassed. With the tested
resource set, the alphabetically allocated additions are Anoka, Ashland, Baxter,
Dennison, Dundas, Eagan, Gilroy and Hampton. Menu placement follows the native
contest list, not necessarily alphabetic event names; the scripted solo route
selects Battle one entry above Jump Race on Dennison.

Course following, its native ABI, solo eligibility decision and limitations
are documented in [Battle navigation](BATTLE_NAVIGATION.md).

## Native map and event unlocking

`UnlockAll` is enabled by default. It writes the existing feat masks at
`0x003D18E0` and `0x003D18E4`, seven track-prize bytes at
`0x004A8AF8..0x004A8AFE`, and event-selection override `0x003D8180=1`.
The latter two operations mirror native `0x002CBC18` and `0x002CD418`;
`0x002CD4A8` consumes the override. Only seven bytes belong to the prize
masks; the adjacent bytes must remain unchanged. The full career cheat
`0x002B6DB8` is not called because it also changes money, vehicles and
career state. With `UnlockAll=false`, these fields are left to native progression.

Home's `hidden=until_career_done` gate uses
`0x002C71B0 → 0x002E0AF8 → 0x00205368(7)` and the feat masks. Home has a
native multiplayer Battle descriptor in `homebase_eves.val`,
`$0069$contest`, with `max_cars=2`, `terrain_mask=64`, and
`terrain_disable_mask=128`. With its inherited terrain bits, the final
native mask is 341. This corrects the older claim that Home had no Battle data.
Unlocking a track does not by itself validate custom bot navigation on it.

The resource display-name list includes Anoka, Ashland, Baxter, Dennison, Dundas,
Eagan, Gilroy, Hampton, Hastings, Home, Kenyon, Mankato, Welch and Woodly.
Do not infer menu tap counts from that list: the actual multiplayer journey
uses nine RIGHT taps to reach Woodly; ten wrapped to Anoka in the captured run.
Home's sixteen native multiplayer contests put Battle last, while Woodly's
25-contest list places Battle at native index 15 (zero based). These menu
contracts are used by the scripted input journey, without selecting maps by
writing arbitrary runtime state.

## Live evidence and remaining validation

Automated runs use isolated memory cards, Vulkan 1x, FrameSkip=0, muted audio,
original force/radius scales of one, and all optional gameplay flags disabled
for the vanilla baseline. `tools/test_battle.sh` saves exact configuration,
controller scripts, captures, trace and final RAM under ignored local output.
Its exit check only establishes reaching combat, not full player acceptance.

- `vanilla-battle` (7,000 vblanks): two native humans, two cars, phase 0→1,
  flags `0x09`, independent movement, visible chickens and arming/reload UI.
  This does not establish exhaustive camera-angle or blast-credit fidelity.
- `mixed-2` (9,000 vblanks): two humans plus two AI, four valid weapon interfaces,
  native phase 0→1, bot movement/firing/ramming, and a bot credited two kills.
  Screenshots show both human wrecks and the native SELECT respawn prompt.
  The automated inputs in this run did not press SELECT, so no human respawns
  should be inferred. One bot remained near its initial area, motivating further
  recovery-policy validation.
- `single-3` (10,000 vblanks, exit 0): Battle selected from Dennison's solo
  menu, one human in slot 3 and three AI in slots 0–2. All bots moved over
  100 world units from their initial positions, fired native weapons, scored
  kills and completed two observed death→respawn cycles each. Human SELECT
  inputs produced two observed respawns. Maximum net scores were 2, 3 and 3
  for the AI. These are sampled trace counts, not an exhaustive shot log.
- `mixed-final` (18,000 vblanks, exit 0): two humans and two bots;
  both bots fired, scored and completed two observed respawns. Maximum
  displacements were 183.16 and 223.35 world units, with maximum net scores
  2 and 3. The match **did not reach phase 2**. Both human input schedules
  ended before the run ended, leaving wrecked humans unrespawned; the bots
  continued, but later showed poor progress near obstacles. This is evidence
  of a navigation limitation, not complete-match acceptance.
- `home-1` (12,000 vblanks, exit 0): rendered Home/native `homebase.trk`,
  two humans/two bots, phase 0→1, bot maximum alive-period displacements
  139.42/268.47, sampled fire transitions 2/6, maximum net scores 1/1,
  observed bot respawns 0/1. The longest throttled interval within three
  units was 7.17/2.33 seconds. This baseline precedes course following;
  its native course cache was empty, so Home uses direct-pursuit fallback.
  It establishes attacks and movement around the Home layout, not a finished
  match or obstacle-clearance guarantee.
- `woodly-route` (12,000 vblanks, exit 0): WOODLY remained selected in
  captures and native `Afton.trk` loaded. Two humans/two bots reached phase
  0→1. Bot maximum alive-period displacement was 234.42/190.36, sampled

  Course telemetry was valid in 114 samples per bot; only slot 1 used routing
  in five samples (native t=92.409–96.413), with direct interception elsewhere.
  The longest throttled interval within three units was 10.01/5.34 seconds.
  Captures show the farmyard, native chickens, moving opponents and fence pins.
  The run **did not reach phase 2**. This proves bounded course activation and
  combat on Woodly, not general obstacle avoidance or completed map acceptance.
- `dennison-route` (15,000 vblanks, exit 0): native `Dennison.trk`,
  two humans/two bots, phase 0→1. Bot maximum alive-period displacements

  and respawns 0/2. Course following activated in 3/27 of 171/168 sampled
  bot updates. Longest throttled intervals within three units were 11.34/3.67

  not reach phase 2, and pins remain. Different stimuli/frame bounds prevent

- `anoka-lifecycle` (18,000 vblanks, exit 0): verified `Anoka.trk`, two
  humans/two bots using the final course policy. Native phase 2 began at
  t=188.322; bot slot 1 reached five net kills (slot 0 maximum four). Both
  bots and both humans completed three sampled respawns each. Bot maximum
  alive-period displacements were 143.12/159.39, firing transitions 11/12,

  score reset followed. Thus five-kill/results acceptance is verified on Anoka,

- The navigation rebuild passed **54/54 CTests** (13.32 seconds, final safe rebuild), including the
  138 native weapon assertions. The local macOS app rebuilt successfully and
  passed `codesign --verify --deep --strict`. Final bundled startup reached

  writing zero to drivetrain engagement left bots nearly stationary. Those

## Current optional-weapon toggle limits

Progression unlocks do not activate cheat flags. `UnlockAll` and native Extras
unlock masks are separate from the active flags at `0x003C4190`. Battle supplies
its native weapon regardless of progression/Extras menu availability; the
locked-progression vanilla journey verifies flags `0x09` and firing.

While the optional Chicken Fight setting is on, each vblank forces master and
weapon (`0x09`) and clears mortar/rain (`0x90`), selecting straight native fire.
Initial OFF leaves native Battle/feat selections alone. OFF after ON preserves
Battle's weapon bit; outside Battle it clears weapon `0x08` unless rain `0x80`
is active. It does not restore the previous mortar/rain selection, and the
master bit remains latched. The rain shortcut's OFF branch clears only `0x80`,
so master/weapon can remain active while the Chicken Fight checkbox is false.
These are known ownership limitations; the stopped redesign was not shipped.
Native rain has priority over mortar, then straight launch; straight-mod ON
suppresses both alternate modes. Turbo and chickens share L2 and may operate
together when both are enabled.

For human cars, the common native world builder at `0x00210000` calls
`0x00227EE8 → 0x00227CA0` for Human records (`0x50`) when `0x002CE180` permits
it; that gate is a native constant-zero return. The factory builds a BALL scene
and queues native physical initialization without a Battle/progression/active
weapon-flag condition. This supports enabling an already constructed weapon
without manual allocation. Static inspection and a historical non-Battle dump
support this; fresh current-build Action/Career live-toggle acceptance and the
actual Extras menu visual state were not completed.

## ps2/DETAIL_PRESETS
# Rendering detail presets

## Player success and scope

Original must preserve the game's image, memory changes and native settings.
High should delay car simplification; Maximum should retain the highest permitted
loaded car model throughout the supported visible race range, including split
screen. Maximum's optional 2P projection/fog range restoration must show complete
geometry without new holes and retain playable native 1x speed; 4x is a separate
performance gate. This does not promise new assets, infinite terrain, persistent
debris, or unchanged performance on every track/hardware.

## Situation and recovered evidence

shows far=575 with configured draw distance1150 and native selected car indexes
1..4. Function00211318 indexes `{1,1,2,2}` using view-count minus1, so the car
LOD multiplier is the same for1P and2P, not doubled in2P. Camera builder00212B58
divides configured distance by view-count and derives both projection and fog
from that quotient. These are distinct causes of detail/range reduction.

Native minimum index is1 for the observed cars. Index0 is not their highest
complete playable car; force-LOD0 would lose geometry/parts. The existing loader
hook already validates table ownership, levels, minimum, model handles and
ordered finite thresholds, respecting clone sharing and native register effects.

## Implementation and research

Reuse the existing `EOD_CAR_LOD_MULTIPLIER` mechanism, also published as
[bf6a575](https://github.com/catsandsoup/eod-recomp/commit/bf6a575) on the optional
`upstream/car-lod-multiplier` branch. A numeric environment override takes
precedence over the whole Detail preset, including range, allowing exact Original
comparison via value1. No change is posted to the upstream repository.

`[Video] Detail=original|high|maximum` defaults to Original and requires restart.
High multiplies positive car thresholds by3. Maximum scales the first native
permitted threshold to at least1,000,000 scaled distance units (>800x the largest
native far plane1150), preserving ordered finite distances and native minimum,
count, handle arrays, flags, wheel/damage logic and shadow tables. Invalid tables
remain unchanged. This retains the highest permitted model for normal finite
visible race distances; it does not bypass culling or force a numeric model0.

Maximum also scopes a2x configured-distance input only around native camera
builder00212B58 when view-count is exactly2 and the input is finite in(0,1150].
Native projection and fog both receive the original1P range. The source distance
word is then restored exactly, preserving guest registers and unrelated callers.
Cinematic overrides and unsupported view counts remain native. No global view
count is forged, no frustum test is bypassed, and no streaming pool is expanded.

Rechecked RoadTripAdventure-recomp's
[overrides.cpp](https://github.com/silentsudin/RoadTripAdventure-recomp/blob/0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8/src/game/overrides.cpp): its camera/frustum changes
are scoped to verified consumers. Its runtime ABI and game addresses differ, and
it has no transferable generic EOD car-LOD implementation. Follow the scoped
consumer pattern using the existing EOD hook and native camera/fog calculation.

Debris persistence and extra1P-only visual passes are excluded: the prior trace
found a per-view12.5/count budget and fixed pool initialization around00310000,
not a proven safe lifetime-only switch. A1P-only call at00218D24 also has
unresolved semantics. Changing global view count to unlock these would affect
simulation/resource limits. Persistent debris needs pool ownership/recycling,
collision, lifetime and exhaustion evidence first. Existing debris/physics,
texture promotion and track traversal remain native.

## Validation

Results follow the bounded, headless/muted build and game gates; no physical
hardware/player acceptance is implied by CPU contracts or one scripted scene.

- Release build and signed Mac app succeeded. All 47 CTest cases pass, including
  eight LOD runtime modes, full guest-memory Original identity, native minimum
  boundaries, invalid thresholds and camera range/view-count boundaries.
- Maximum completed the scripted 6600-vblank two-player race at both 1x and 4x,
  headless and muted. Native 640x448 race windows: median59.9, minimum59.3 FPS.
  At4x (2560x1792 internal), last six five-second race windows: median58.55,
  minimum49.3 FPS. Loading/countdown also dips into the low50s. Maximum therefore
  does NOT meet a locked60FPS 4x gate; it remains optional and Original remains
  the default. These are window averages, not instantaneous minimums.
- Native Maximum trace:640 model-selection samples retained native minimum1,
  visible distances through431 units, far plane1150;20 valid car tables loaded.
  Both players take distinct scripted paths. Reviewed captures show complete
  nearby cars/damage and more complete distant cars; no obvious holes or fog
  seams in this bounded scene. Other tracks/physical play remain unverified.
- Replaying the identical baseline GS capture on unmodified8e74d28 and candidate
  produced byte-identical4MiB VRAM and2560x1792 screenshots. Separate live
  Original runs did not produce identical hashes; full live-run byte identity
  is not claimed. CPU contracts prove the disabled hook's memory behavior;
  same-capture replay establishes renderer parity, not game-hook execution.

## ps2/GAMEPLAY_MODS_RE
# Test Drive: Eve of Destruction (SLUS-209.10) - Gameplay Mods & Reverse Engineering Technical Reference

> [!WARNING]
> **Correction — 2026-10-19:** This document contains historical claims that are
> not a verified implementation contract. Read [Battle recovery](BATTLE_RECOVERY.md)
> first for the checked native weapon ABI and current evidence limits. In

> pointers; `0x0017E000` is the trigger and `0x0017E5C8` is an update;
> flag `0x10` selects the feat mortar rather than the straight Battle shot.
> Earlier steering, synthetic weapon registration, bot recovery guarantees,
> respawn relocation and world-origin boundary claims must not be used as proof
> of correct native behavior. The new chapter distinguishes verified CPU results
> from pending gameplay validation and supersedes conflicting statements below.

## Executive Summary & Agent Handoff

This technical reference document provides an exhaustive reverse-engineering specification, memory map, disassembly breakdown, mathematical AI formulation, and user guide for gameplay modifications and the Battle Mode subsystem within the static recompilation of *Test Drive: Eve of Destruction* (`SLUS_209.10` / `eod-recomp`).

The systems documented herein encompass:
1. **Master Feats & Career Cheats Unlocking**: Permanent career unlock states, bitmask layout at `0x003C4190`, career-mode lockout bypass, and concurrent multi-cheat activation.
2. **High-Velocity Scaled Turbo Boost Thrust Engine**: Interception of `HumanDriver::DriveUpdate` (`f_0018F2A8`), bypass of the hardcoded 100 mph (44.44 m/s) velocity ceiling, and linear forward impulse injection.
3. **Explosive Ballistic Chicken Shockwave Engine**: Projectile kinematics of the `Ball` object (`0x228` bytes), radial impulse scaling in `f_0017DA58`, and spatial hash grid interaction.
4. **Single-Player & Multi-AI Battle Mode Architecture**: Full reverse engineering of event type `0x18000224`, master event tables (`0x003C3A70`), contest tables (`0x003C61A8`), Eve tables (`0x003C4D08`), EveResultsTracker (`0x003C4BF8`), the `BattleMaster` core structure (`0x5AC` bytes), vehicle input setters (`f_0018AA50-80`), and weapon accessors (`f_0017DE78`/`f_0017E5C8`).
5. **Demolition Derby AI Combat Subsystem**: Mathematical formulations for dynamic lead-pursuit trajectory interception, power-slide ramming via rear-wheel handbrake modulation, 40-frame barrier unstick recovery state machine, ballistic chicken weapon firing geometry, 1P-to-4P dynamic bot scaling, 5-kill race finish arbitration, and arena infield respawn/boundary reflection physics.
6. **Zero-Friction Controller-Only User Journey**: Chording combos (`L1+R1+DPad`, `L3+R3`, Hold `Select`), chord button suppression in IOP pad RPC, and multi-sensory feedback (haptic pulses, audio chimes, HUD banners).
7. **Configuration & Verification Reference**: Unified `eod.ini` schema, environment variable overrides, headless padscript automation, and CTest regression test execution.

---

## 1. Feature 1: Cheats & Career Unlocks Architecture

### 1.1 Memory Map & Bitmasks

#### Active Gameplay Cheat Mask: `0x003C4190` (`uint32_t`)
The master gameplay bitmask is evaluated at runtime during vehicle physics ticks, controller input sampling, and collision damage evaluation:

| Bit | Hex Value | Name in `feats.val` | Description | EE Disassembly Sites |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **0** | `0x001` | *Master Cheat Enable* | Master gate. Must be set for any cheat to activate during gameplay. Set in Arcade; **cleared in Career Mode**. | `0x0018F47C`, `0x0018FC1C`, `0x0017E628`, `0x002C1224` |
| **1** | `0x002` | `turbo_boost` (`hack=1`) | Turbo Boost on holding L2 button. | `0x0018F488` |
| **2** | `0x004` | `hardcore_mode` (`hack=2`) | Hardcore realistic deformation / structural damage scaling. | `0x00188BDC`, `0x0018EFFC` |
| **3** | `0x008` | *Weapon Master Active* | Enables L2 weapon triggering, missile trajectory updates, and reticle tracking. | `0x0017E4EC`, `0x0018FC28`, `0x001AF99C` |
| **4** | `0x010` | `horn_ball` (`hack=4`) | Chicken Fight (launches forward ballistic explosive chicken from vehicle nose). | `0x0017E25C`, `0x0017E634`, `0x0017F314` |
| **5** | `0x020` | `ai_vengeance` (`hack=5`) | Demolition Derby AI drivers aggressively seek and ram player vehicle. | `0x00193B20`, `0x001985D0` |
| **6** | `0x040` | `leader_takes_damage` (`hack=6`) | First place vehicle continuously accumulates structural damage over time. | `0x001B5BD0` |
| **7** | `0x080` | `raining_chickens` (`hack=7`) | Explosive chickens drop from high altitude directly above all active vehicles. | `0x0017E228`, `0x0017E6CC`, `0x0017F2E0` |
| **8** | `0x100` | `one_hit_kills` (`hack=8`) | Any collision impact exceeding threshold instantly totals vehicle (`damage = 1.0f`). | `0x0018D7D4`, `0x00204A40` |
| **9** | `0x200` | `sepia` (`hack=9`) | Vintage sepia visual post-processing color grading filter. | `0x0017868C`, `0x002378F4`, `0x00268930` |

#### Feat Unlock Memory Registers
- `0x003D18E0` (`uint32_t`): Bitmask of career-completed feats (`0..7`).
- `0x003D18E4` (`uint32_t`): Cheat feat unlock bitmask. Function `f_00205218()` writes `0xFFFFFFFF` to unlock all feat cheats in the Feats menu.
- `0x003D80E0` (`int32_t[8]`): Current toggle states (`0 = off`, `1 = on`) for the 8 UI cheat menu entries.

### 1.2 The Career Mode Lockout Vulnerability & Bypass
In vanilla `SLUS_209.10`, entering any Career Mode race triggers `f_002C1224`:
```mips
002c1224 lw   $v1, 0x4190($s0)     ; load active cheat mask from 0x003C4190
002c1228 andi $v0, $v1, 0xFFFE     ; CLEARS BIT 0 (Master Cheat Enable)!
002c122c sw   $v0, 0x4190($s0)     ; write back stripped mask
```
Because bit 0 is cleared, every subsequent cheat check (`andi $v0, $v1, 0x1; beq $v0, $zero, skip`) fails across vehicle physics and weapons.
**Recomp Engine Bypass**: `src/game_patches.cpp:game_patches_vblank()` asserts `cheats |= 0x1` every vblank whenever `career_cheats` or any live mod is enabled, permanently neutralizing the career lockout.

### 1.3 Concurrent Turbo Boost & Chicken Weapon Execution
In the stock PS2 UI, selecting Chicken Fight disabled Turbo Boost and vice versa because the UI table `0x003D80D8` paired `{0x18, 0x80}` to avoid conflicting over the single `Ball` projectile pool.
In the underlying physics engine:
- Turbo Boost is evaluated at `0x0018F488` via bit `0x02`.
- Weapon Firing is evaluated at `0x0018FC28` via bit `0x08` and `0x10`.
Both inspect the L2 button independently. By setting `0x003C4190 |= 0x1B` (Master `0x01` + Turbo `0x02` + Weapon Master `0x08` + Horn Ball `0x10`), holding L2 initiates maximum forward rocket thrust while continuously launching ballistic explosive chickens.

### 1.4 Master Career Unlock Sequence (`f_002B6DB8`)
Calling `f_002B6DB8()` executes the engine's internal completion routines:
- `f_0012CF98()`: Unlocks all career tier tracks, vehicles, and reputation prizes.
- `f_00205218()`: Unlocks all 8 feat prizes (`0x003D18E4 = 0xFFFFFFFF`).
- `f_002CD418()`: Unlocks all eve events across all venues.
- `f_002E06A0()`, `f_002E09C8()`, `f_002E0098()`: Unlocks all Dare challenges and championships.

---

## 2. Feature 2: High-Velocity Scaled Turbo Boost Thrust Engine

### 2.1 Code Location: `f_0018F2A8` (`HumanDriver::DriveUpdate`)
Vehicle physics updates are executed in `f_0018F2A8` (`0x0018F2A8`–`0x0018FBA0`).
- Argument `$a0` (`$s2`): Pointer to `VehicleController`
  - `+0x38`: Pointer to `Car` rigid body object
  - `+0x3C`: Pointer to `DriverInput` interface
  - `+0x40`: `int32_t car_index`

### 2.2 Forward Velocity Projection
The engine projects the 3D linear velocity vector onto the vehicle heading vector:
```mips
0018f33c addiu  $a1, $v1, 0x104     ; car->velocity (Vector3: X=0x104, Y=0x108, Z=0x10C)
0018f340 addiu  $a2, $v1, 0x7C      ; car->forward_heading (Vector3: X=0x7C, Y=0x80, Z=0x84)
...
0018f368 madd.s $f22, $f5, $f4      ; $f22 = dot(velocity, forward) -> forward speed (m/s)
```

### 2.3 Force Multiplier & Rigid Body Injection
When L2 is depressed:
```mips
0018f4b8 lui   $at, 0x3FC0          ; 1.5f (base boost force multiplier)
0018f4bc mtc1  $at, $f21
...
0018f5cc lui   $at, 0x46EA
0018f5d0 ori   $at, $at, 0x6000     ; 30,000.0f Newtons (base thrust force)
0018f5d4 mtc1  $at, $f12
0018f6a4 lwc1  $f0, 0x1B88($a2)     ; car mass factor
0018f6a8 mul.s $f0, $f0, $f12      ; 30,000.0f * mass
0018f6ac mul.s $f0, $f21, $f0      ; * 1.5f = 45,000.0f * mass
```
Impulse application is completed by calling `f_0017B708(car, force_vec, offset_vec)`.

### 2.4 The Hardcoded 100 mph (44.44 m/s) Top Speed Cap & Bypass
```mips
0018f508 lui   $at, 0x4231
0018f50c ori   $at, $at, 0xC71D     ; 0x4231C71D = 44.444447f m/s (exactly 100.0 mph)
0018f510 mtc1  $at, $f2             ; speed ceiling register
...
0018f550 c.lt.s $f22, $f2           ; compare forward speed ($f22) with 44.444447f
0018f558 bc1f   L_skip_boost        ; IF SPEED >= 100 MPH, DISENGAGE BOOST ENTIRELY!
```
**Recomp Engine Scaling**: In `src/game_patches.cpp:f_0018F2A8()`, the recompiled driver multiplies the thrust impulse by `g_config.turbo_scale` (default `1.75f`) and expands the speed ceiling:
$$v_{\text{cap}} = 44.444447\text{ m/s} \times \text{turbo\_scale}$$
At `turbo_scale = 1.75`, $v_{\text{cap}} \approx 77.78\text{ m/s}$ (174.0 mph).

---

## 3. Feature 3: Explosive Ballistic Chicken Detonation & Shockwave Physics

### 3.1 Projectile Kinematics (`Ball` Object, `0x228` Bytes)
- Projectile Vtable: `0x003F9528` / `0x003F9538`
- Sound FX bindings: `chkstart.sfx` (launch cluck), `chkroll.sfx` (ground bounce), `explode.sfx` (detonation blast).
- Initial launch kinematics computed in `f_0017EC58`:
  $$\vec{v}_{\text{launch}} = \vec{v}_{\text{car}} + (0.707\vec{f} + 0.495\vec{u}) \times 24.89\text{ m/s}$$
  where $\vec{f}$ is the vehicle forward vector (`car + 0x7C`), $\vec{u}$ is the upward normal (`car + 0x70`), and $\vec{v}_{\text{car}}$ is linear velocity (`car + 0x104`).

### 3.2 Detonation Handler: `f_0017E718`
Upon contact with a vehicle rigid body or terrain boundary:
```mips
0017e79c lui   $at, 0x40F0          ; 0x40F00000 = 7.5f meters (BLAST RADIUS)
0017e7a0 mtc1  $at, $f20
...
0017e7e8 lui   $at, 0x46C3
0017e7ec ori   $at, $at, 0x5000     ; 0x46C35000 = 25,000.0f Newtons (BLAST FORCE)
0017e7f0 mtc1  $at, $f13
0017e7f4 mov.s $f12, $f20           ; argument $f12 = blast radius (7.5m)
0017e7fc jal   func_17DA58          ; f_0017DA58(pos=$s0, attacker=$a1, radius=$f12, force=$f13)
```

### 3.3 Shockwave Function & Spatial Hash Grid: `f_0017DA58`
`f_0017DA58(const float *pos, int attacker_car_idx, float radius, float force)`:
1. Queries the 100×100 2D spatial hash grid at `0x0048D2B4` (cell size 8m×8m) using the explosion epicenter `(pos[0], pos[2])`.
2. Gathers dynamic physics bodies in the 4 adjacent spatial buckets.
3. Computes radial impulse distance $d = \|\vec{P}_{\text{car}} - \vec{P}_{\text{blast}}\|$.
4. For all bodies within $d \le \text{radius}$:
   $$\vec{F}_{\text{impulse}} = \text{force} \times \left(1.0 - \frac{d}{\text{radius}}\right) \times \frac{\vec{P}_{\text{car}} - \vec{P}_{\text{blast}}}{d}$$
   Deformation damage is simultaneously applied to `car + 0x1BEC`.
**Recomp Engine Scaling**: In `src/game_patches.cpp:f_0017DA58()`, radius and force arguments are scaled by `g_config.chicken_radius_scale` (default `1.5f` $\rightarrow$ 11.25m) and `g_config.chicken_force_scale` (default `2.0f` $\rightarrow$ 50,000 N).

---

## 4. Feature 4: Single Player & Multi-AI Battle Mode Architecture

### 4.1 Master Event Table (`0x003C3A70`) & Bitfield Structure
In `SLUS_209.10`, the event registry resides at `0x003C3A70`. Entries have a 12-byte stride (`0xC`), terminated by `event_type == 0`:

```
+0x00: uint32_t event_type
+0x04: uint32_t name_string_ptr        (e.g., "battle", "normal_race")
+0x08: uint32_t display_name_string_ptr (e.g., "Battle", "No-Rules Race")
```

#### Event Registry Dump
| Index | Event Type Hex | Name String | Display Name String | Category |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **0** | `0x00002110` | `"normal_race"` | `"No-Rules Race"` | Race |
| **4** | `0x01002105` | `"figure8_race"` | `"Figure-8"` | Race |
| **17** | `0x18000215` | `"soccer"` | `"Soccer Match"` | Arena / Minigame |
| **23** | `0x1800421c` | `"save_ring"` | `"Survival"` | Arena Elimination |
| **24** | `0x1880221e` | `"kill_derby"` | `"Demolition Derby"` | Arena Elimination |
| **26** | `0x18802220` | `"kill_push"` | `"Push-Off"` | Arena Elimination |
| **27** | `0x18802221` | `"kill_knock"` | `"Knock-Out"` | Arena Elimination |
| **28** | `0x18006222` | `"capture"` | `"Capture the Flag"` | Arena Minigame |
| **30** | `0x18000224` | `"battle"` | `"Battle"` | Multi-Car Arena Combat |

#### Event Helper Functions
- `f_0010AFA0(uint32_t event_type)`: Iterates `0x003C3A70`, returns `display_name_string_ptr`. If missing, panics at `0x0010AFE0`: `"race: can't find event type for 0x%x"`.
- `f_0010AF28(const char *name)`: Performs `strcmp` against `+0x04`, returning `event_type`.
- `f_0010B000(uint32_t event_type)`: Returns internal identifier string (e.g. `"battle"`).

#### Event Bitflags
- `event_type & 0x00000100` (Race Flag): Tested at `0x0012415C` in `f_00123B98`. If bit `0x100` is 0 and contest is Contest 0 of an Eve in Career Mode, the engine panics: `"Eve %s, first contest must be a race"`.
- `event_type & 0x00000800` (Trailer Flag): Tested at `0x001243F0` (`cars * 2 <= 20`).
- `event_type & 0x18000000` (Arena Category): Handled in Arena Master Factory `f_001D97B0`. At `0x001D993C`, tests `(event_type & 0xFFFF) == 0x0224`, branching to `0x001D9948` which instantiates `BattleMaster` (`0x5AC` bytes) via constructor `f_00166C60`.

### 4.2 In-Memory Eve & Contest Tables
- **Eve Table**: Base `0x003C4D08`, Stride `0x84`, count at `0x003C4CF4` (`num_eves`):
  - `+0x00`: `int32_t eve_index`
  - `+0x04`: `int32_t league_index`
  - `+0x08..+0x27`: `char track_name[32]` (e.g. `"Dennison"`)
  - `+0x28..+0x67`: `char eve_display_name[64]`
  - `+0x70`: `uint32_t num_contests` (number of contests in this Eve)
- **Contest Table**: Base `0x003C61A8`, Stride `0x28`, count at `0x003C4CF8` (`num_contests`, capacity 320):
  - `+0x00`: `uint32_t global_index`
  - `+0x04`: `uint32_t eve_index`
  - `+0x08`: `uint32_t event_type` (`0x18000224` for Battle Mode)
  - `+0x0C`: `uint32_t laps` (`1`)
  - `+0x10`: `uint32_t max_cars` (`4` - strictly bounded by `BattleMaster`)
  - `+0x14`: `uint32_t terrain_mask` (`0xFFFFFFFF`)
  - `+0x18`: `uint32_t rounds` (`1`)
  - `+0x1C`: `uint32_t purse` (`500`)
  - `+0x20`: `uint32_t name_table_ptr` (layout override, e.g. `"c_battle"`)
  - `+0x24`: `uint32_t enabled` (`1` = active/selectable in carousel)

### 4.3 Carousel UI Rendering & `EveResultsTracker` (`0x003C4BF8`)
The Action Mode event selection carousel is driven by `f_00379728`:
- Mode dispatcher `f_00379CA8` queries `f_002DE250()`. If 0, calls `f_00379728` (Action Mode); if 1, calls `f_00378E50` (Career Mode).
- Format string `"Event %d of %d"` is stored at `0x0042D588` and referenced at `0x0037993C`:
  ```mips
  0037994c jal  f_00120C50       ; verify active eve
  00379954 jal  f_00120D78       ; returns current_event_idx (0-based) from EveResultsTracker
  00379958 addiu $s0, $v0, 0x1   ; s0 = current_event_idx + 1 (1-based)
  0037995c lw   $a0, 0x1854($sp) ; destination string buffer
  00379960 daddu $a1, $s1, $zero ; format: "Event %d of %d" (0x0042D588)
  00379964 daddu $a2, $s0, $zero ; %d = current_event_idx + 1
  00379968 jal  f_003A7068       ; sprintf(dest, "Event %d of %d", cur, total)
  0037996c daddu $a3, $v0, $zero ; %d = total_events (from f_00120DA8)
  ```
- **List Construction Loop** (`0x003797F8`–`0x00379868`):
  Iterates `s3 = 0` to `num_events - 1`: queries contest pointer via `f_00125388(contest_idx)` (`0x003C61A8 + c * 0x28`), extracts `contest->event_type` (`+0x08`), resolves display name via `f_0010AFA0()`, and stores into carousel array `$sp + 0x12B0 + s3 * 0x80`.
- **Injection Hook**: Intercepting `f_001244A8` appends Battle Mode (`0x18000224`) and configures Contest 0 of Eve 0 to Battle Mode, causing "Event 1 of 5" in the Action Mode carousel to directly boot Battle Mode.

### 4.4 Controller Query & 1-Player Solo Clean Boot
- Physical controller query: `f_00335518` counts connected pads.
- Callers of `f_00335518`:
  - `0x002C0DF4`: Main Menu Multiplayer verification. Branches to `0x002A3220` displaying dialog `"Multiplayer requires at least two controllers!"` (`0x004197B8`).
  - `0x002B8E1C`: Player setup screen. Clamps player count to 1 if count $&lt; 2$.
- **Solo Clean Boot Rationale**: When Battle Mode is launched via Single Player Action Mode (`mode == 0x12F`) or Career Mode (`mode == 0x130`), the code branch at `0x002C0DF4` is **never executed**.
- **Respawn Safety**: In `f_001673B8` (respawn selector), when `num_cars == 1` (`total_opponents == 0`), the opponent distance loop executes 0 times and assigns spawn point at `0x00167518` without null dereferences. 1 player drives solo cleanly.

### 4.5 `BattleMaster` Object Memory Layout (`0x5AC` Bytes)
Allocated at `0x00167F4C` via `f_0012E870`, constructed via `f_00166C60`:

| Offset Range | Type | Field Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `+0x00` | `uint32_t` | `vtable` | Vtable pointer (`0x003F7770` / `0x003F5BB8`). |
| `+0x04` | `int32_t` | `event_state` | Match progression: `0` = countdown, `1` = active combat, `2` = match finished / victory. |
| `+0x08` | `uint32_t` | `saved_cheats` | Preserved cheat mask from `0x003C4190`. |
| `+0x0C` | `uint32_t` | `flag` | Internal state flags. |
| `+0x10..+0x450` | `struct[16]` | `respawns[16]` | 16 Arena Respawn records (`0x44` bytes each). |
| `+0x450` | `int32_t` | `num_respawns` | Total valid respawn points parsed (default 16). |
| `+0x454..+0x594` | `struct[4]` | `cars[4]` | **Per-Car Battle State Array** (4 cars max, stride `0x50` = 80 bytes). |
| `+0x594..+0x5A4` | `int32_t[4]` | `place[4]` | Sorted rankings: car indices for 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th place. |
| `+0x5A8` | `int32_t` | `num_cars` | Total participant cars in the match (1 to 4). |

#### Per-Car Battle State Struct (`0x50` Bytes per slot `i`):
- `+0x454 + i*0x50`: Slot status flags (`0` = empty, `1` = active/spawned).
- `+0x460 + i*0x50`: Hits dealt / kills (`int32_t`, incremented at `0x00167084`).
- `+0x468 + i*0x50`: Hits taken / deaths (`int32_t`, incremented at `0x00167198`).
- `+0x46C + i*0x50`: Net score (`int32_t`, calculated as `kills - deaths` at `0x00167F8C`).

#### Respawn Point Record (`0x44` Bytes per slot `k`):
- `+0x00`, `+0x04`, `+0x08`: Right vector $(R_x, R_y, R_z)$
- `+0x0C`, `+0x10`, `+0x14`: Up normal vector $(U_x, U_y, U_z)$
- `+0x18`, `+0x1C`, `+0x20`: Forward heading vector $(F_x, F_y, F_z)$
- `+0x24`, `+0x28`, `+0x2C`: Spawn coordinate $(P_x, P_y, P_z)$
- `+0x30`: In-use flag
- `+0x34`: Distance rating to nearest opponent

> [!CAUTION]
> The `BattleMaster` structure is strictly dimensioned for 4 cars (`0x454 + 4 * 0x50 = 0x594`). Attempting to register `num_cars > 4` writes past the per-car array, directly corrupting `place[4]` (`+0x594`) and `num_cars` (`+0x5A8`).

### 4.6 Global Active Pointers & Memory Map Reference
The following global addresses govern the runtime Battle Mode session:

| Global Address | Type | Identifier | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0x003CF194` | `uint32_t*` | `g_battle_master` | Pointer to active `BattleMaster` instance. Non-null during battle. |
| `0x003CF19C` | `uint32_t` | `cur_event_type` | Current event type (`0x18000224` when Battle Mode is executing). |
| `0x003C41AC` | `uint32_t` | `num_players` | Number of active human viewports (`1` = full screen, `2..4` = splits). |
| `0x0048522C` | `uint32_t` | `num_cars` | Active vehicle count participating in the current physics world. |
| `0x00447458` | `uint32_t[4]` | `g_car_array` | Pointers to active `Car` rigid bodies. Indexable via `f_00179A08(i)`. |
| `0x003C3A6C` | `uint32_t*` | `g_session_mgr` | Session Manager struct pointer; offset `+0x18` stores player count. |

### 4.7 Vehicle Input Control Setters & Rigid Body Offsets
AI controllers inject input into vehicles using the native engine control setters:

```
f_0018AA50(Car *car, int gear)         -> Stores transmission gear into car + 0x1B90 (1 = forward, -1 = reverse)
f_0018AA80(Car *car, float steer)      -> Stores steering ratio into car + 0x1B6C ([-1.0f, +1.0f])
f_0018AA70(Car *car, float gas)        -> Stores throttle into car + 0x1B70 ([0.0f, 1.0f])
f_0018AA68(Car *car, float footbrake)  -> Stores footbrake into car + 0x1B74 ([0.0f, 1.0f])
f_0018AA60(Car *car, float handbrake)  -> Stores handbrake into car + 0x1B78 ([0.0f, 1.0f])
```

#### Calling Conventions (MIPS Register State):
- Argument 1 (`$a0` / `g_ee.r[4]`): Target vehicle pointer (`Car*`).
- Argument 2 (`$a1` / `g_ee.r[5]` for `f_0018AA50`): Integer gear (`1` or `-1`).
- Argument 2 (`$f12` / `g_ee.fpr[12]` for steer, gas, brake, handbrake): Single-precision float.

#### Car Rigid Body Memory Offsets (`SLUS_209.10`):
- `car + 0x64`, `+0x68`, `+0x6C`: Right unit vector $\vec{R} = (R_x, R_y, R_z)$
- `car + 0x70`, `+0x74`, `+0x78`: Up normal unit vector $\vec{U} = (U_x, U_y, U_z)$
- `car + 0x7C`, `+0x80`, `+0x84`: Forward heading unit vector $\vec{F} = (F_x, F_y, F_z)$
- `car + 0x88`, `+0x8C`, `+0x90`: World coordinates $(P_x, P_y, P_z)$
- `car + 0x104`, `+0x108`, `+0x10C`: Linear velocity vector $(V_x, V_y, V_z)$
- `car + 0x1B88`: Vehicle chassis mass factor ($m$)
- `car + 0x1BEC`: Cumulative structural damage ratio ($D \in [0.0f, 1.0f]$)

#### Wheel Friction Physics: Handbrake (`0x1B78`) vs Footbrake (`0x1B74`)
Analysis of `f_00189D50` (tire slip & longitudinal traction update) reveals critical physics divergence:
- **Footbrake (`car + 0x1B74`)**: Applies retarding torque to all four wheels, killing forward velocity and clamping wheel rotational angular velocity $\omega \to 0$.
- **Handbrake (`car + 0x1B78`)**: Uncouples front wheels, zeroing front braking torque, and locks only the rear axle. When applied at speed during steering deflection, rear tire cornering stiffness drops to zero ($C_{\alpha,\text{rear}} \approx 0$), initiating an oversteer yaw rotation while engine throttle (`0x1B70 = 1.0f`) maintains forward velocity.

### 4.8 Weapon Subsystem Functions


- `f_0017DDB0(Weapon *weapon)`: Unregisters and removes a weapon from the registry.
- `weapon->vtbl[2] (`weapon, car, &trigger_state`, source checkout)`: Native virtual method (`*(weapon->vtbl + 8)`) executed each tick within `HumanDriver::DriveUpdate` (`f_0018F2A8_orig`) when Chicken Fight cheat is active.
- `f_0017DA58(const float *pos, int attacker_idx, float radius, float force)`: Applies explosion impulse and radial chassis deformation.

## 5. Feature 5: Demolition Derby AI Mathematical Models & Physics Formulations

### 5.1 Lead-Pursuit Interception Trajectory Modeling
Direct target tail-chasing in open demolition arenas results in AI vehicles constantly trailing behind moving opponents. Lead-pursuit interception models the future collision point based on target linear velocity:

```
         (Lead Point)
           (x_lead, z_lead)
              * <---------------+ (Target: tpx, tpz, tvx, tvz)
             /                   \
            /                     \
    (Displacement L)               \
          /                         \
         /                           \
        * (AI Car: ax, az, avx, avz)
```

#### Formulation:
1. **Closing Velocity Vector**:
   $$v_{\text{closing}} = \|\vec{V}_{\text{ai}}\| + 12.0\text{ m/s}$$
2. **Estimated Time-to-Interception**:
   $$t_{\text{lead}} = \text{clamp}\left(\frac{d_{\text{target}}}{v_{\text{closing}}}, 0.0\text{ s}, 1.2\text{ s}\right)$$
   where $d_{\text{target}} = \sqrt{(P_{x,\text{target}} - P_{x,\text{ai}})^2 + (P_{z,\text{target}} - P_{z,\text{ai}})^2}$.
3. **Predicted Lead Coordinates**:
   $$x_{\text{lead}} = P_{x,\text{target}} + V_{x,\text{target}} \cdot t_{\text{lead}}$$
   $$z_{\text{lead}} = P_{z,\text{target}} + V_{z,\text{target}} \cdot t_{\text{lead}}$$
4. **Lead Displacement Vector**:
   $$\vec{L} = (x_{\text{lead}} - P_{x,\text{ai}}, z_{\text{lead}} - P_{z,\text{ai}})$$
   $$\hat{L} = \frac{\vec{L}}{\|\vec{L}\|}$$
5. **Steering Error Projection**:
   Projecting $\hat{L}$ onto the AI vehicle right unit normal $\vec{R} = (R_x, R_z)$ gives the lateral steering deflection:
   $$steer\_dot = \hat{L} \cdot \vec{R} = L_x R_x + L_z R_z$$
   $$steer = \text{clamp}(steer\_dot \times 2.2f, -1.0f, +1.0f)$$
6. **Wrecked Target Filtering**:
   Active targets are evaluated in priority order. Vehicles with $D \ge 1.0f$ (`ee_rf(tc + 0x1BEC) >= 1.0f`) are flagged wrecked/respawning and skipped, ensuring bots pursue operational opponents.

### 5.2 Power-Slide Ramming & Handbrake Lateral Drift Dynamics
To execute high-speed T-bone collisions rather than glancing rear-end scrapes, bots execute power-slides on sharp cornering angles:

#### Activation Criteria:
$$face\_dot &lt; 0.15 \quad \text{AND} \quad \|\vec{V}_{\text{ai}}\| > 9.0\text{ m/s}$$
where $face\_dot = \hat{L} \cdot \vec{F} = L_x F_x + L_z F_z$.

#### Control Modulation:
- **Handbrake**: Set to `0.90f` via `f_0018AA60()` on `car + 0x1B78`.
- **Footbrake**: Explicitly set to `0.0f` via `f_0018AA68()` on `car + 0x1B74`.
- **Gas / Throttle**: Maintained at `1.0f` via `f_0018AA70()` on `car + 0x1B70`.
- **Exit Condition**: When $face\_dot \ge 0.15$ or speed drops below $9.0\text{ m/s}$, handbrake is reset to `0.0f`.

#### Physics Outcome:
Rear axle traction breaks, generating an aggressive yaw moment $\tau_{\text{yaw}} = I_z \ddot{\psi}$. The vehicle slides sideways into the interception path at a $60^\circ$–$90^\circ$ T-bone collision angle while retaining full engine momentum.

### 5.3 Barrier Unstick Recovery State Machine
When an AI vehicle strikes a perimeter wall or barrier at an acute angle, full throttle pins the nose, resulting in zero progress.

```
       [ Normal Driving ]
              |
              | aspeed < 1.4 m/s && moved_d < 0.35m
              v
       [ Pin Accumulator ] (stuck_frames++)
              |
              | stuck_frames > 40 (~0.67s)
              v
       [ Reverse Recovery ] (reverse_frames = 55, ~0.92s)
              |
              | reverse gear = -1, gas = 1.0, steer = reverse_dir * 0.9
              v
       [ Unstick Complete ] (< 2.0s Total Elapsed Time)
```

#### Mathematical Specification:
1. **Displacement Metric**:
   $$\Delta d = \sqrt{(P_{x,t} - P_{x,t-1})^2 + (P_{z,t} - P_{z,t-1})^2}$$
2. **Pin Detection Threshold**:
   $$\|\vec{V}_{\text{ai}}\| &lt; 1.4\text{ m/s} \quad \text{AND} \quad \Delta d &lt; 0.35\text{ m}$$
3. **Trigger Threshold**:
   If the pin condition holds for $> 40\text{ frames}$ ($\approx 0.67\text{ s}$ at 60Hz):
   - Set `reverse_frames = 55` ($\approx 0.92\text{ s}$).
   - Determine reverse escape steering:
     $$\text{reverse\_dir} = (steer\_dot \ge 0.0f) \; ? \; -1 \; : \; +1$$
4. **Recovery Control State**:
   - `gear = -1` via `f_0018AA50()`
   - `gas = 1.0f` via `f_0018AA70()`
   - `steer = reverse_dir * 0.9f` via `f_0018AA80()`
   - `footbrake = 0.0f`, `handbrake = 0.0f`
5. **Recovery Timing Verification**:
   Total recovery duration $= 40 + 55 = 95\text{ frames} = 1.583\text{ seconds}$, guaranteed to satisfy the $&lt; 2.0\text{ s}$ acceptance requirement.

### 5.4 Ballistic Chicken Weapon Targeting & Firing Geometry
AI vehicles scan direct line-of-sight toward their current target:

#### Targeting Metrics:
- Direct displacement vector: $\vec{D} = \vec{P}_{\text{target}} - \vec{P}_{\text{ai}}$
- Direct distance: $d_{\text{direct}} = \|\vec{D}\|$
- Direct facing dot product:
  $$direct\_face\_dot = \frac{\vec{D} \cdot \vec{F}}{\|\vec{D}\|} = \frac{D_x F_x + D_z F_z}{d_{\text{direct}}}$$

#### Firing Gate:
$$\begin{cases}
direct\_face\_dot > 0.70 & (\text{Target within } \pm 45.5^\circ \text{ heading cone}) \\
8.0\text{ m} \le d_{\text{direct}} \le 45.0\text{ m} & (\text{Safe lethal ballistic range}) \\
\text{cooldown} \ge 65\text{ frames} & (\ge 1.08\text{ s between rounds})
\end{cases}$$

- **Lower Bound (8.0m)**: Protects the firing bot from entering its own scaled explosion blast radius ($R_{\text{blast}} \approx 11.25\text{ m}$).
- **Upper Bound (45.0m)**: Prevents wasting projectiles beyond realistic parabolic flight range.
- **Combat Execution**:
  AI vehicles in demolition derby and battle mode focus on full-throttle lead interception ramming and power-slide oversteer maneuvers, driving opposing vehicles into barrier walls and triggering physics deformation without relying on corruptible weapon slots.

### 5.5 Dynamic Multi-Player Bot Scaling (1P to 4P)
The engine allocates AI controllers exclusively to non-human participant slots:

#### Allocation Formula:
$$ai\_idx \in [num\_players, num\_cars - 1]$$
where $num\_players = \text{clamp}(ee\_r32(0x003C41AC), 1, 4)$.

| Game Mode | $num\_players$ | Slot 0 | Slot 1 | Slot 2 | Slot 3 | Active AI Bots |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **1-Player Solo** | 1 | Human P1 | AI Bot 1 | AI Bot 2 | AI Bot 3 | **3 AI Bots** |
| **2-Player Split** | 2 | Human P1 | Human P2 | AI Bot 1 | AI Bot 2 | **2 AI Bots** |
| **3-Player Split** | 3 | Human P1 | Human P2 | Human P3 | AI Bot 1 | **1 AI Bot** |
| **4-Player Split** | 4 | Human P1 | Human P2 | Human P3 | Human P4 | **0 AI Bots** |

This dynamic allocation ensures human player controller ports are never overridden while maintaining a full 4-car demolition grid across all modes.

### 5.6 5-Kill Victory Arbitration & Post-Match Scoreboard Guard
The 5-kill victory condition is natively executed in `BattleMaster::Update` (`f_00167D58` in `SLUS_209.10:0x00167D58`–`0x00167E28`):
```mips
00167d78 lw    $v0, 0x4($s0)       ; battle_master->event_state
00167d7c bne   $v0, $v1, exit      ; $v1 = 1 (active match)
00167d84 lw    $v0, 0x5A8($s0)     ; num_cars
...
00167dac lw    $v0, 0x0($a0)       ; kills = car[i].kills
00167db0 lw    $v1, 0x0($a1)       ; deaths = car[i].deaths
00167db4 subu  $v0, $v0, $v1       ; net_score = kills - deaths
00167db8 slti  $v0, $v0, 0x5       ; net_score < 5 ?
00167dbc bne   $v0, $zero, next    ; continue checking cars
00167dc4 addiu $v0, $zero, 0x2
00167dc8 sw    $v0, 0x4($s0)       ; battle_master->event_state = 2 (MATCH OVER!)
00167de8 jal   func_167658         ; f_00167658: sort participant scores into place[4]
00167e04 addiu $a0, $s0, 0x594     ; place array (1st to 4th rankings)
00167e08 jal   func_201938         ; f_00201938: display post-match scoreboard!
```

#### Match State Guarding:
In `src/game_patches.cpp`, the AI update loop is strictly guarded:
```cpp
uint32_t event_state = ee_r32(bm + 0x04);
if (event_state == 1) {
    // Execute AI pursuit, sliding, unstick, and chicken weapons
}
```
- **Countdown (`event_state == 0`)**: AI controllers remain silent; cars rev on grid without steering away before green flag.
- **Victory / Results (`event_state == 2`)**: AI controllers immediately relinquish control, allowing `f_00167658` score sorting and `f_00201938` 1st-to-4th place results presentation to render without interference.

### 5.7 Arena Infield Respawns & Kinetic Boundary Reflection
Demolition Derby tracks feature tight enclosed infields, whereas stock Battle Mode tables spawned cars on the outer multi-mile speedway.

#### Track Survey: `c_battle.va0` vs `c_kill_derby.va0`
- `c_battle.va0` spawns vehicles at radius $\sim 106\text{m}$ on open raceways with zero boundary fences.
- `c_kill_derby.va0` has a 16-point boundary polygon ($\approx 44\text{m} \times 52\text{m}$) but **lacks `[respawn]` sections**, triggering immediate panic at `0x00167B54`: `"battle: must have at least 4 respawn points"`.

#### Recomp Infield Respawn Relocation:
At match initialization, all 16 respawn points (`battle_master + 0x10 + i * 0x44`) are relocated within the Demolition Derby infield circle:
$$r_i = 12.0\text{ m} + ((i \% 4) \times 1.5\text{ m}) \quad \in [10.0\text{ m}, 18.0\text{ m}]$$
$$\theta_i = i \times \frac{2\pi}{N_{\text{respawns}}}$$
$$P_{x,i} = r_i \cos(\theta_i), \quad P_{z,i} = r_i \sin(\theta_i)$$
Forward heading is oriented toward the center:
$$\vec{F}_i = (-\cos(\theta_i), 0.0, -\sin(\theta_i))$$

#### Kinetic Boundary Clamping:
For all active vehicles, perimeter distance $d = \sqrt{P_x^2 + P_z^2}$ is monitored every vblank:
```
           Boundary Radius R = 24.5m
             .-'""'-.
           .'   n    '.
          /     ^      \
         |      |       |
         |      * Car   |
         |     (px, pz) |
          \            /
           '.        .'
             '-....-'
```
If $d > 24.5\text{ m}$:
1. Compute inward unit normal $\hat{n} = \left(-\frac{P_x}{d}, -\frac{P_z}{d}\right)$.
2. Calculate normal velocity component $v_n = \vec{V} \cdot \hat{n}$.
3. If $v_n &lt; 0$ (vehicle moving outbound):
   $$\vec{V}' = \vec{V} - (1.0 + e) \cdot (\vec{V} \cdot \hat{n}) \cdot \hat{n}$$
   with restitution coefficient $e = 0.8$ ($1.0 + e = 1.8$), bouncing the car back into the arena.
4. Position is clamped to perimeter safety limit:
   $$P_x' = -\hat{n}_x \times 24.0\text{ m}, \quad P_z' = -\hat{n}_z \times 24.0\text{ m}$$

## 6. Feature 6: Zero-Friction Controller-Only User Journey & Mod Chording

### 6.1 Live Controller Combos Matrix
Cheats and gameplay modes can be toggled in real time during live driving or while paused without navigating submenus:

| Controller Trigger | Action | Resulting Cheats & Memory State |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`L1 + R1 + D-Pad UP`** | Chicken Fight (Horn Missile) | Forward explosive chicken projectile on L2 (`0x003C4190 |= 0x19`). |
| **`L1 + R1 + D-Pad RIGHT`** | Turbo Boost | Forward acceleration rocket impulse on L2 (`0x003C4190 |= 0x03`). |
| **`L1 + R1 + D-Pad DOWN`** | Raining Chickens | Explosive chickens drop from sky above cars (`0x003C4190 |= 0x89`). |
| **`L1 + R1 + D-Pad LEFT`** | AI Vengeance & Hardcore | Demolition AI pursuit (`0x20`) + realistic deformation (`0x04`). |
| **`L1 + R1 + Triangle`** | Chaos Mode | Simultaneous Chicken Fight + Turbo Boost on L2 (`0x003C4190 |= 0x1B`). |
| **`L1 + R1 + Select`** | Quick Chicken Toggle | Immediately inverts `cheat_chickens` state. |
| **`L3 + R3`** (Both Sticks Click) | Instant Chicken Fight Toggle | Toggles `cheat_chickens` on the fly. |
| **Hold `Select` (30 frames / 500ms)** | Instant Chicken Fight Toggle | Toggles `cheat_chickens`. Short tap (&lt;30 frames) retains normal vehicle reset. |
| **`L1 + R1` (Hold)** | Live Cheat Guide Overlay | Renders on-screen cheat guide HUD overlay. |
| **Keyboard `F5`** | Chicken Fight Toggle | Toggles forward ballistic chickens. |
| **Keyboard `F6`** | Turbo Boost Toggle | Toggles high-velocity turbo boost. |
| **Keyboard `F7`** | Raining Chickens Toggle | Toggles aerial chicken drop. |
| **Keyboard `F8`** | Chaos Mode Toggle | Toggles Chaos Mode (Chickens + Turbo). |

### 6.2 Button Suppression & Steering Protection
To eliminate accidental driving twitches or pause menu disruptions while executing combos:
- `game_patches_suppressed_buttons()` returns the active combo mask:
  `PAD_L1 | PAD_R1 | PAD_UP | PAD_DOWN | PAD_LEFT | PAD_RIGHT | PAD_TRIANGLE | PAD_SELECT | PAD_L3 | PAD_R3`
- In `runtime/iop/pad.cpp:write_pad_data()`, these buttons are masked out of port 0 pad data before sending to the PS2 engine.
- **Result**:
  - While racing: holding `L1+R1` and pressing D-Pad Left/Right will not steer the car into a wall.
  - While paused: pressing D-Pad Up/Down will not move the pause cursor or accidentally select "Quit".
  - Holding `Select` for recovery does not trigger car reset upon releasing the chicken toggle.

### 6.3 Multi-Sensory Feedback Engine
1. **Timed Haptic Pulse**: `platform_haptic_pulse(0, 150, 1, 180)` triggers an isolated 150ms rumble pulse, immune to physics loop cancellation.
2. **Dual-Tone Synthesized Audio Chime**: `platform_audio_feedback(bool enabled)` generates an 80ms PCM chirp (ascending 880Hz $\to$ 1320Hz for ON; descending 880Hz $\to$ 440Hz for OFF) submitted to `platform_audio_submit`.
3. **Visual HUD Banner**: Renders `★ CHICKEN FIGHT: ON (Press L2 to Fire) ★` for 2500ms on the display buffer.

## 7. Configuration Matrix & Deployment Guide

### 7.1 Unified `eod.ini` Settings Reference
The recompilation engine reads settings from `eod.ini` located in the application directory:

```ini
[Cheats]
UnlockAll=true               ; Unlocks all career tracks, vehicles, and feat cheats
CareerCheats=true            ; Enables cheat execution in career mode races
SinglePlayerBattle=true      ; Injects Battle Mode into Single Player Action & Career carousels
TurboBoost=false             ; Enables Turbo Boost by default
ChickenFight=false           ; Enables Chicken Fight by default
TurboScale=1.75              ; Multiplier for turbo thrust acceleration & top speed cap
ChickenForceScale=2.0        ; Multiplier for chicken detonation impulse force
ChickenRadiusScale=1.5       ; Multiplier for chicken explosion blast radius

[Display]
Aspect=16:9                  ; Display aspect ratio: 4:3, 16:9, 16:10, stretch
Fullscreen=false             ; Fullscreen window toggle
InternalResolution=1         ; Rendering scale multiplier (1x = 640x448, 6x = 3840x2688)

[Audio]
MasterVolume=100             ; Master audio output volume (0 to 100)
Mute=false                   ; Global audio mute toggle
```

All INI settings can be overridden at runtime via environment variables:

| `EOD_SP_BATTLE` | `Cheats.SinglePlayerBattle` | `bool` | `true` | Injects Battle Mode contest into Eve 0 / 1. |
| `EOD_TURBO` | `Cheats.TurboBoost` | `bool` | `false` | Enables Turbo Boost on startup. |
| `EOD_CHICKENS` | `Cheats.ChickenFight` | `bool` | `false` | Enables Chicken Fight on startup. |
| `EOD_TURBO_SCALE` | `Cheats.TurboScale` | `float` | `1.75` | Scales turbo acceleration and speed ceiling. |
| `EOD_CHICKEN_FORCE` | `Cheats.ChickenForceScale` | `float` | `2.0` | Scales explosion blast impulse Newtons. |
| `EOD_CHICKEN_RADIUS` | `Cheats.ChickenRadiusScale`| `float` | `1.5` | Scales blast radius damage meters. |

## 8. Verification, Test Harness & Forensic Audit Protocol

### 8.1 Headless Emulation & Padscript Syntax
Automated testing is driven via `tools/padscript.py` and the engine's headless CLI:

```bash
# Generate Padscript tokens (FRAME:BUTTON)
```
